decisions_this_run: D-080a: expose revocation as its own endpoint rather than a filter on the holdings report. The holdings view answers 'who holds what now'; revocation is history. Two questions, two answers, so no reader has to infer state from nullable columns.

D-080b: reuse the operator-access-report scope instead of minting a new one. Reading the removal history is the authority the holder report already needs; a fifth token would require every auditor to be granted twice for one question.

D-080c: treat 'revoked_at set, revoked_by NULL' as a valid post-deletion state and enforce only 'named revoker must have an instant'. A CHECK that ignores ON DELETE SET NULL makes the referenced account undeletable, which is a worse failure than the incoherence it prevents.

D-080d: move the 'configuration grant must not invent a reason' rule from the domain constructor to the write paths (IssueOperatorGrant requires it, the configuration seed forbids it). A domain invariant that the database itself can produce makes every read fail.
run_summary: Run 80 delivered NEX-080: an operator can now read the platform's grant-removal history. NEX-079 wrote revoked_at/revoked_by onto the grant row so that 'who removed whose authority, and when' was answerable, but nothing surfaced it - a durable write with no read, the same half-built loop NEX-076/NEX-077 closed for rationale. GET /api/v1/ops/operator-grants/revoked returns it under the existing operator-access-report scope (no fifth token), and the holdings report carries both fields. Running the neighbouring suites found two NEX-079 defects, both from ON DELETE SET NULL: the revocation CHECK made any account holding revocation history undeletable, and the domain's granter/rationale pairing turned one account deletion into an outage of the whole /ops surface. Migration a91c6f0d4b27 fixes the CHECK; the pairing rule moved to the write paths. 1619 passed / 4 skipped, ruff+mypy clean, migration round-trips.
